events.heading: GA51 — Committee on Constitutional Business advice on Overture 6 (minutes excerpt)
events.action_text:
- **E.** Overture 6 from the Presbytery of Susquehanna Valley: "Amend BCO Sections to Require Background Checks for Church Office"

In the opinion of the CCB, Overture 6, particularly the language “shall obtain and review," is in conflict with (1) WCF 23.3 because, insofar as it adds a requirement for Presbytery to obtain something that the civil magistrate might withhold or abolish, it cedes to the civil magistrate an effective authority he may not assume, namely, the right to deny admittance to the body of Christ and (2) BCO Preliminary Principle II in that it deprives members of the church of the right to determine who shall be admitted to its communion.

events.heading: GA52 — CCB advice on Overture 1
events.action_text:
In the opinion of the CCB Overture 1 is in conflict with the Constitution in the following ways:
• The proposed amendment creates a conflicting constitutional threshold regarding the nature of an offense that is subject to judicial process. Specifically, Overture 1 requires that "the alleged offense rises to a level warranting judicial process," but, according to BCO 29- 1, the "proper object of judicial process” is “anything in the doctrines or practice of a Church member professing faith in Christ which is contrary to the Word of God";
• The proposed amendment creates a conflicting constitutional threshold regarding the standard of proof required to commence judicial process when charges are presented by a voluntary prosecutor. Specifically, Overture 1 requires that there must be "a strong presumption of guilt" (proposed BCO 32-2.e.) and (assuming the list is conjunctive) that “it is reasonable to expect the offense can be proven through judicial process" (BCO 32-2.f.), but BCO 31-9 only requires "probable cause" for charges from a voluntary prosecutor; and
• The proposed amendment removes agency from someone seeking to become a voluntary prosecutor. Specifically, the logic of the Rules of Discipline presumes that individuals have the right to bring charges and prosecute them voluntarily (see, e.g., BCO 31-6, -7, -9), but Overture 1 places an absolute investigatory and high moral burden on the court in every case where charges are laid before the court by an individual.

Additionally, in the opinion of CCB, Overture 1 is ambiguous in that it is unclear whether the items listed are conjunctive or disjunctive. Adopted 8-0-0
events.outcome: CCB identified constitutional conflicts and ambiguity; advice adopted 8-0-0.

events.heading: GA52 — CCB advice on Overture 22
events.action_text:
In the opinion of the CCB, Overture 22 is in conflict with Preliminary Principle 6 and BCO 6-4, in that PP6 affirms that "the power to elect persons to the exercise of authority in any particular society resides in that society" and BCO 6-4 acknowledges that every communicant member is “entitled to all the rights and privileges of the church," while the proposed BCO 25-1 grants congregations the right to remove a communicant member's right and privilege to vote.

CCB notes that adopting this change would create collateral consequences regarding the quorums specified in BCO 25-2, -3. Adopted 8-0-0
events.outcome: CCB found conflict with Preliminary Principle 6 and BCO 6-4; advice adopted 8-0-0.

events.heading: GA52 — CCB advice on Overture 25
events.action_text: In the opinion of the CCB, Overture 25 is in conflict with BCO 13-1 and 13- 2 in that it applies permissive language to a Teaching Elder holding membership in his Presbytery; further, it creates a constitutional conflict by using mandatory language requiring all Honorably Retired Teaching Elders to hold associate membership in a local congregation. To the extent the language of the proposed amendment is deemed to apply to existing Honorably Retired Teaching Elders, it appears to be in conflict with Preliminary Principle 2. Finally, the Overture uses the phrase “communicant fellowship” which is a category undefined by our Constitution. Adopted 8-0-0
events.outcome: CCB found conflict with BCO 13-1 and 13-2 and Preliminary Principle 2; advice adopted 8-0-0.

events.heading: GA52 — CCB advice on Overture 30
events.action_text:
In the opinion of the CCB, Overture 30 is in conflict with our Constitution in that it purports to give Presbyteries authority over the installation of Teaching Elders to calls outside of churches of the Presbytery and the PCA as well as the dissolution of such calls.

Additionally, in the opinion of the CCB, Overture 30 is ambiguous regarding the relation between a “needful work" (BCO 8-4) and “a work not under the jurisdiction of his Presbytery" (BCO 13-2; cf. BCO 13-5), which is often called an “out of bounds call." It is unclear whether a “needful work" encompasses all “out of bounds calls," or whether there is still a category of “out of bounds calls" that are different from “needful works." Adopted 8-0-0
events.outcome: CCB found constitutional conflict and ambiguity; advice adopted 8-0-0.

events.heading: GA52 — CCB advice on Overture 32
events.action_text:
In the opinion of the CCB, Overture 32 is ambiguous in that it is not clear whether the "hearing" in the added paragraph is governed by other provisions in the Rules of Discipline, such as BCO 32-10, -13, -15, -16, -17, -18; and BCO 35, and whether the accused has the right to Appeal an elevated suspension.

CCB notes that the phrase “original trial court” is potentially ambiguous in that it is not clear if the phrase refers to the exact commission or group of presbyters who heard the evidence at the original trial; whether the phrase refers simply to the Session or Presbytery in which the trial was held; or whether the phrase could include another court that has assumed jurisdiction under BCO 37-7.

CCB also notes that this overture is in conflict with Overture 38. Adopted 8-0-0
events.outcome: CCB identified ambiguity and conflict with Overture 38; advice adopted 8-0-0.

events.heading: GA52 — Administrative Committee advice on Overtures 3 and 4
events.action_text: 3. That the Overtures Committee receive the following advice on Overture 3 from Arizona Presbytery, "Erect Ad Interim Committee on Christian Nationalism," and Overture 4 from South Texas Presbytery, "Erect Ad Interim Committee on Christian Nationalism." The Administrative Committee offers no opinion per se on the wisdom of the proposed study committee. In the event the Assembly answers Overtures 3 and 4 in the affirmative, approving the establishment of an ad interim committee on the study of Christian Nationalism, the budget of such committee be set at a maximum of $10,000, provided solely by designated gifts to the AC. The AC notes: "Funding should not be the burden primarily of the members of the ad interim committee nor the AC, but of those requesting the ad interim committee. Any overture proposing an ad interim committee should ordinarily include a plan for how sufficient, designated funds for the ad interim committee will be raised." (RAO 9-3) The AC further notes "only two (2) ad interim committees may be appointed or continued in any given year, unless additional ones are approved by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Assembly" (RAO 9-3) Any study committee approved without a funding plan requires a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the General Assembly as an amendment to the AC budget (RAO 9-3, 4-11). Since the AC can only administer funds that have been designated and received for an ad interim study committee (RAO 9-3), funds will be distributed by the AC only as they are made available in the project account.
events.outcome: offered no opinion on whether the committees should be created; if approved, advised a $10,000 maximum funded solely by designated gifts to the AC and cited RAO funding limits.

events.heading: GA52 — Administrative Committee advice on Overtures 3 and 4
events.action_text: 3. That the Overtures Committee receive the following advice on Overture 3 from Arizona Presbytery, "Erect Ad Interim Committee on Christian Nationalism," and Overture 4 from South Texas Presbytery, "Erect Ad Interim Committee on Christian Nationalism." The Administrative Committee offers no opinion per se on the wisdom of the proposed study committee. In the event the Assembly answers Overtures 3 and 4 in the affirmative, approving the establishment of an ad interim committee on the study of Christian Nationalism, the budget of such committee be set at a maximum of $10,000, provided solely by designated gifts to the AC. The AC notes: "Funding should not be the burden primarily of the members of the ad interim committee nor the AC, but of those requesting the ad interim committee. Any overture proposing an ad interim committee should ordinarily include a plan for how sufficient, designated funds for the ad interim committee will be raised." (RAO 9-3) The AC further notes "only two (2) ad interim committees may be appointed or continued in any given year, unless additional ones are approved by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Assembly" (RAO 9-3) Any study committee approved without a funding plan requires a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the General Assembly as an amendment to the AC budget (RAO 9-3, 4-11). Since the AC can only administer funds that have been designated and received for an ad interim study committee (RAO 9-3), funds will be distributed by the AC only as they are made available in the project account.
events.outcome: offered no opinion on whether the committees should be created; if approved, advised a $10,000 maximum funded solely by designated gifts to the AC and cited RAO funding limits.
